title: Phrasal Verbs & Idiomatic Expressions

blueprint.instruction: Use the following phrasal verbs and idiomatic expressions (Language expressions) in sentences of your own.

phrasalVerbs.example: The bus broke down on the way to school.
The students carried out an experiment.
We checked in at the hotel.

phrasalVerbs.meaning: leave a hotel after staying there
phrasalVerbs.example: We checked out of the hotel in the morning.

phrasalVerbs.meaning: entered slowly with a heavy sound
phrasalVerbs.example: The train chugged into the station.
The writer drew upon his experience.
The car drove off quickly.
Please fill in the application form.

idiomaticExpressions.example: The baker gave us a baker’s dozen of buns.

idiomaticExpressions.expression: All’s fair in love and war
idiomaticExpressions.meaning: anything may be considered acceptable in difficult competition or conflict
idiomaticExpressions.example: He believed that all’s fair in love and war.

idiomaticExpressions.meaning: make people feel comfortable in a new situation
idiomaticExpressions.example: The teacher told a joke to break the ice.

idiomaticExpressions.meaning: praise someone to gain their favour
idiomaticExpressions.example: He tried to butter his teacher up before asking for help.
The manager calls the shots in the company.
Cat got your tongue? Why aren't you answering?
The two brothers are like chalk and cheese.
It crossed my mind that I had forgotten my book.
His mistake left him with egg on his face.

idiomaticExpressions.meaning: something extra that makes a good situation even better
idiomaticExpressions.example: Winning the prize was the icing on the cake.
We travelled through the length and breadth of the country.
The shopkeeper suspected that the customer was light-fingered.

idiomaticExpressions.meaning: gone for a long time / no longer present
idiomaticExpressions.example: When we arrived, the bus was long gone.

idiomaticExpressions.expression: Not to lose heart / lose one's heart
idiomaticExpressions.meaning: not to become discouraged / become deeply attracted
idiomaticExpressions.example: Do not lose heart when you face difficulties.
When the children arrived, out came the treats.
The boy quaked in his boots when he saw the snake.
It was raining cats and dogs yesterday.
